subject: Attribution Model Question
body:
Hi Polaris Support,

Hope you're having a good week. 

I'm reaching out because I'm trying to get a clearer understanding of how Polaris calculates attribution for our campaigns. We're looking at the data coming in from our Google Ads and GA4 accounts, and I'm trying to reconcile some of the reported conversions and their sources. 

Specifically, I'm wondering which attribution model Polaris uses by default. We've explored a few different models in GA4 itself (like data-driven and last-click), and I want to make sure I'm comparing apples to apples when looking at the Polaris dashboards. 

Is there a way to see which model is being applied, or if it's configurable within Polaris? We're on the Enterprise plan, and I want to make sure we're leveraging all the features to their fullest potential. Understanding this will really help us in optimizing our ad spend and understanding true customer journeys.

Thanks in advance for any information you can provide.

Best,
A Polaris User
response:
Hi there,

Thanks for reaching out! Great question—attribution modeling is crucial for optimizing ad spend effectively.

**Polaris uses multi-touch attribution by default**, which shares credit across all touchpoints a customer interacted with before converting. This is different from GA4's last-click or data-driven models, so that's an important distinction when reconciling numbers between the two platforms. Multi-touch gives you a more complete picture of what actually drives revenue, rather than crediting only the final touchpoint.

**To view your attribution and choose your model:**
1. Go to **Dashboards** and select or create a dashboard
2. Add an **Attribution** widget
3. Choose your model and date range
4. You'll see credit distribution across your campaigns

This should let you see which model is being applied and configure it as needed for your analysis.

One thing to note: for attribution to work properly in Polaris, you'll want to make sure you have:
- GA4 connected (for user interaction tracking)
- Your CRM synced (HubSpot or Salesforce)
- UTM parameters on all paid ads
- Your email platform connected if you want email touchpoints included

If you're still seeing discrepancies or have questions about configuring attribution specifically for your Enterprise setup, I'd recommend contacting our support team directly—they can dive deeper into your account configuration.

Best of luck optimizing your campaigns!

subject: Attribution report is blank??
body: Hey, why is my attribution report totally empty? I'm missing data here and I need this to work. Did something break or do I need to connect something else?
response:
Let me help you troubleshoot your empty attribution report. Here are the most common causes:

**1. Missing UTM parameters**
Make sure you've added `utm_source`, `utm_medium`, and `utm_campaign` to your ad links. Without these, Polaris can't attribute clicks to your campaigns.

**2. Connectors aren't active**
Check that your GA4 and/or CRM connectors are connected and active. You can verify this in **Workspace Settings > Connectors**. If authentication has expired, you'll need to reconnect.

**3. Data sync timing**
Attribution syncs on your workspace schedule (hourly or daily). If you just set things up, new conversions will appear in the next sync cycle.

body: hey, quick question about attribution. i'm on the starter plan and trying to get a better handle on how our google ads and ga4 data are being attributed in polaris.  i've been poking around the dashboards and reports, but i'm not totally clear on which model polaris uses by default.  do you guys lean towards last-click, or is it something more sophisticated like linear or data-driven?  we're really trying to figure out what's driving actual conversions, you know?  just want to make sure we're not misinterpreting the numbers based on the attribution.  any chance you could point me to where i can find that info, or just tell me what the default is?  thanks.
response:
Great question! Polaris uses **multi-touch attribution**, which is more sophisticated than last-click. Here's what that means for you:

Instead of crediting only the last touchpoint before a conversion (like Google Ads does by default), Polaris **shares credit across all the touchpoints a customer interacted with** before converting. This gives you a much more complete picture of what's actually driving your revenue.

To see your attribution data:
1. Go to **Dashboards** and select or create a dashboard
2. Add an **Attribution** widget
3. Choose your model and date range
4. You'll see credit distribution across your campaigns

**To get attribution working**, you'll need:
- GA4 connected (to track interactions on your site)
- UTM parameters on all your paid ads (so Polaris can identify which campaign, source, and medium drove each click)
- Your CRM synced (HubSpot or Salesforce) to map interactions to actual deals/revenue

Since you're already looking at Google Ads + GA4 data, you're on the right track. Just make sure your UTM parameters are set up consistently across your ads, and your CRM is synced so Polaris can tie everything back to actual conversions.

If you run into issues setting this up or have questions specific to your Starter plan, feel free to reach out to support!

body:
Hi Polaris Support,

I'm a viewer on the Starter plan and I was hoping you could clarify something for me regarding attribution models. We're trying to get a better understanding of how Polaris attributes conversions, especially when looking at our Google Ads and GA4 data. 

Specifically, I'm wondering which attribution model Polaris uses by default, or if it's something we can choose or customize? Best,
A Polaris User
response:
Hi,

Great question! I'm happy to clarify how Polaris handles attribution.

**Polaris uses multi-touch attribution by default.** This means credit is shared across *all* the touchpoints a customer interacted with before converting — not just the last click or first click. This gives you a more complete picture of what actually drives revenue, since most customers interact with you multiple times before buying.

So rather than giving all credit to a single touchpoint (like Google Ads' last-click model), Polaris shows how your Google Ads, GA4, email, and CRM data all contributed to each conversion.

**Regarding customization:** The knowledge base I have access to shows how to view and choose your attribution model and date range in a dashboard widget, but I don't have details about whether you can switch between different model types or customize the weighting. That may depend on your plan level, so it's worth checking directly or reaching out to our support team for specifics on what's available to Starter plan users.

**On those discrepancies you're seeing:** To make sure Polaris is calculating attribution correctly, you'll want to verify that:
- GA4 is connected
- Your CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce, etc.) is synced
- All your paid ads have **UTM parameters** so Polaris can identify which campaign/source/medium drove clicks
- Your email platform (if used) is connected

If you've set all that up and still see odd numbers, I'd recommend contacting our support team — they can dig into the specifics of your setup.

Hope that helps!

This gives you a more complete picture of what actually drives revenue across your full customer journey.

1. Go to **Dashboards** and select or create a dashboard
2. Add an **Attribution** widget
3. Choose your model and date range
4. You'll see credit distribution across your campaigns

To ensure attribution is working properly, you'll want to confirm you have:
- GA4 connected (tracks user interactions)
- CRM synced (HubSpot or Salesforce, to map interactions to deals/revenue)
- UTM parameters on all paid ads
- Email platform connected (Mailchimp, Brevo, etc.)

If you need more details about the specific models available to choose from beyond multi-touch attribution, I'd recommend contacting our support team directly — they can walk you through all the options available on your Enterprise plan.

Hope this helps!
